record.original_question: Find an example of a nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, meaning an action that produces a family of inequivalent Poisson structures not related by a coordinate change.

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem to find an example of nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, thus spreading it to a family of inequivalent structures not related by a coordinate change.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional affine real manifold with coordinates $x = (x^1,\dots,x^n)$, and let $\mathcal{P}(M)$ denote the space of Poisson bivectors on $M$, i.e. bivector fields $P = \tfrac12 P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i\wedge\partial_j$ satisfying $[\![P,P]\!] = 0$ with respect to the Schouten bracket. The Kontsevich graph complex $\mathsf{GC}_2$ is the differential graded Lie algebra of formal $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combinations of isomorphism classes of finite undirected graphs (with ordered edges, modulo sign), with differential given by vertex expansion. A cocycle $\gamma \in \ker d \subset \mathsf{GC}_2$ on $n$ vertices and $2n-2$ edges produces, via the orientation morphism $\mathrm{Or}\colon \mathsf{GC}_2 \to T_{\mathrm{poly}}(M)$, a bivector-valued map $Q_\gamma\colon \mathcal{P}(M) \to \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ such that for every Poisson bivector $P$, $[\![P, Q_\gamma(P)]\!] = 0$; equivalently, $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ is an infinitesimal symmetry preserving the Poisson property. Two such infinitesimal deformations $Q,Q'$ of $P$ are equivalent (a Poisson coboundary) if there exists a vector field $X$ on $M$ with $Q - Q' = [\![P, X]\!]$, i.e. they differ by an infinitesimal change of coordinates.

Problem. Exhibit a triple $(M, P, \gamma)$ consisting of a finite-dimensional affine real manifold $M$, a Poisson bivector $P$ on $M$, and a nontrivial Kontsevich graph cocycle $\gamma \in \mathsf{GC}_2$ such that the induced infinitesimal deformation $Q_\gamma(P)$ of $P$ is not a Poisson coboundary, i.e. there is no vector field $X$ on $M$ with $Q_\gamma(P) = [\![P, X]\!]$. Equivalently, integrating the flow $\dot P_t = Q_\gamma(P_t)$ should yield a one-parameter family of Poisson structures $\{P_t\}$ that are pairwise inequivalent under diffeomorphisms of $M$.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Poisson geometry
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) on the action of Kontsevich graph cocycles on Nambu–Poisson brackets explicitly state that producing a nontrivial graph-cocycle deformation of a Poisson bracket — one yielding a family of inequivalent Poisson structures not related by a coordinate change — remains an open problem. Known cocycles such as the tetrahedron γ₃ and the pentagon/heptagon-wheel cocycles have been shown, in the cases studied, to act as Poisson coboundaries (e.g. the tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in dimensions 2 ≤ d ≤ 4 on Nambu brackets).

status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open problem to find an example of nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, thus spreading it to a family of inequivalent structures not related by a coordinate change.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, II. The tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in 4D
status_evidence.snippet: For 2 ≤ d ≤ 4, the action of the tetrahedron γ₃ on Nambu brackets is a Poisson coboundary.
status_evidence.claim: Standard cocycles act as coboundaries in known examples, leaving the existence question open.

status_evidence.snippet: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a nontrivial cocycle action on a Poisson bracket is listed among open problems.
